skill.name: cookbook-audit
skill.description: Review Anthropic Cookbook notebooks against the project style guide, run automated notebook checks, and produce scored feedback with concrete improvements.
skill.summary: Audit Cookbook notebooks with a rubric, validation script, and actionable review report.
skill.author: anthropics

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are markdown examples, checklist text, or placeholder setup guidance, not active secret access or command execution. The confirmed risk is shell command construction in validate_notebook.py, where notebook paths are interpolated into sh -c strings before running detect-secrets. No evidence found for prompt injection or intentional data exfiltration.

remediation.issue: Shell command construction for secret scanning
remediation.suggestion: Replace sh -c pipelines with subprocess.run argument lists and pass the notebook path as a separate argument. Avoid echo and xargs for user-controlled paths.

remediation.issue: User-supplied notebook path reaches external tools
remediation.suggestion: Resolve the path, require an .ipynb suffix, and reject unexpected locations before invoking nbconvert or detect-secrets.
Keep placeholder examples clearly marked as non-secrets and prefer dotenv loading examples over direct environment assignment examples.

content.value_statement: Notebook reviews can miss narrative, setup, and code-quality issues. This skill applies the Anthropic Cookbook rubric and validation script to produce scored, actionable feedback.
actual_capabilities: Reviews Cookbook notebooks against the included style guide and scoring rubric.
Runs a local validation script when a notebook path is available.
Converts notebooks to markdown for easier manual review.
Checks for hardcoded secrets, noisy install output, model naming, and deprecated API patterns.
Scores narrative quality, code quality, technical accuracy, and actionability.
Produces concrete recommendations with examples and line references when available.
limitations: It is specialized for Anthropic Cookbook notebooks and may not fit other documentation formats.
Automated checks depend on local tools such as uv, nbconvert, and detect-secrets.
It needs access to the notebook file path to run validation.
It does not prove technical correctness beyond the reviewed notebook content.

use_cases.title: Pre-Submission Cookbook Review
use_cases.description: Review a notebook before publishing and get prioritized fixes for structure, setup, and code presentation.

use_cases.title: Editorial Quality Audit
use_cases.description: Apply a consistent rubric across multiple submissions and compare scores across review dimensions.

use_cases.title: Technical Enablement Check
use_cases.description: Find issues that reduce reader success, including missing prerequisites, invalid model names, and unclear conclusions.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Notebook Audit
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review with a single notebook path.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this Cookbook notebook: <path>. Use the standard rubric and list the most important fixes first.

prompt_templates.title: Focused Setup Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review focused on prerequisites and execution readiness.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review <path> for setup quality, dependency clarity, API key handling, and notebook execution issues.

prompt_templates.title: Rubric Score Comparison
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review that compares strengths and weaknesses across dimensions.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit <path> and provide scores for narrative quality, code quality, technical accuracy, and actionability. Include evidence for each score.

prompt_templates.title: Publication Readiness Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Perform a publication readiness audit for <path>. Run automated checks if possible, then give blocking issues, improvements, and suggested rewrites.

output_examples.input: A reviewer asks for an audit of a draft Cookbook notebook about CI failure triage.
output_examples.output: The report gives an overall score, highlights missing learning objectives, flags noisy install output, and recommends a stronger conclusion.

output_examples.input: An author wants to know whether a notebook is ready for publication.
output_examples.output: The audit separates blocking issues from polish items and gives concrete edits for setup, model constants, and explanation before code cells.

output_examples.input: A documentation lead wants consistent feedback across several notebook drafts.
output_examples.output: Each notebook receives the same four-part score, plus comparable notes on narrative structure, technical accuracy, and reader actionability.

best_practices: Provide the notebook path and any review goals before starting the audit.
Review automated findings together with the manual rubric before deciding readiness.
Use the scored sections to prioritize fixes that improve reader success first.
anti_patterns: Using the skill as a general code security scanner for unrelated projects.
Skipping manual review because the validation script produced few warnings.
Applying the Cookbook rubric to notebooks with different audience or publishing standards.

faq.question: What does this skill audit?
faq.answer: It audits Anthropic Cookbook notebooks for narrative quality, setup, code quality, technical accuracy, and actionability.

faq.question: Does it run automated checks?
faq.answer: Yes, when a local notebook path is available and the required tools can run in the environment.

faq.question: Can it find hardcoded secrets?
faq.answer: It attempts to run detect-secrets through the included validation script and also reports fallback pattern matches.

faq.question: Does it replace human review?
faq.answer: No. It structures the review and catches common issues, but technical judgment is still required.

faq.question: What output should I expect?
faq.answer: Expect an executive summary, dimension scores, critical issues, prioritized recommendations, and concrete examples where available.

faq.question: Can Codex or Claude Code use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.
